q: In what year did the author of the novel 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
In which city was the composer of the opera 'The Magic Flute' born?
The first person to walk on the Moon was born in which US state?
Which chemical element has an atomic number equal to the number of the Apollo mission that first landed humans on the Moon?
Which river flows through the capital city of the country that hosted the 1992 Summer Olympics?
Which political party did the US president in office when the Berlin Wall fell belong to?
In which city was the physicist after whom the SI unit of frequency is named born?
The architect of the Sydney Opera House won which major architecture prize, and in what year?
How many natural moons does the planet named after the Roman god of war have?
In what year did the television series of the comedy group that the Python programming language is named after first air?
The first woman to win a Nobel Prize had a daughter who also won one. In which year and in which field did the daughter win?
What is the chemical symbol of the element named after the scientist credited with the first widely recognized periodic table?
In which English county was the author of 'Pride and Prejudice' born?
In what year did the country that gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States adopt the euro as its (non-cash) currency?
Into which sea does the river that flows through Cairo empty?
The film that won Best Picture at the first Academy Awards ceremony held after the Burj Khalifa officially opened was directed by the first woman to win Best Director. In which city was she born?
gold: San Carlos, California (Kathryn Bigelow, The Hurt Locker)

q: By how many metres does the height of Mount Everest announced jointly by China and Nepal in 2020 exceed the figure from the 1955 Survey of India?
Element 109 is named after a physicist whose long-time collaborator alone received a Nobel Prize for their joint discovery. For which year is that Nobel Prize listed?
The UN climate conference (COP) held the year after the one in the United Arab Emirates took place in a capital city on the shore of which body of water?
OpenAI had two interim CEOs in November 2023. The second one had co-founded a live-streaming platform. Which company bought that platform, and in what year?
The mountain whose summit is the farthest point on Earth's surface from Earth's centre is in which country, and who led its first recorded ascent?
The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics was shared by two laureates. The one born in the United Kingdom earned his PhD at which university?
The explorer who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole sailed south on a ship that had earlier carried another explorer's Arctic expedition. Name the ship and that earlier explorer.
The IAU General Assembly that reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet met in a city with a famous medieval astronomical clock. In what year was that clock first installed?
The 2023 film that won Best Picture at the 96th Academy Awards was based on a biography. Which major prize did that biography win, and in what year?
The physicist whose 1905 paper on the photoelectric effect was cited in his Nobel Prize received the prize for which year, and in what year was it actually awarded to him?
The October Revolution in Russia is named for a date in the Julian calendar. On what Gregorian calendar date was the Winter Palace stormed?
gold: Night of 7 to 8 November 1917; the palace fell early on 8 November (26 October Old Style), the uprising began 7 November (25 October)

q: What is the highest air temperature on Earth currently recognised by the World Meteorological Organization, and which earlier record in Libya did the WMO invalidate, in what year?
gold: 56.7 C (134 F), Furnace Creek, Death Valley, 1913; El Azizia 58 C (1922) invalidated in 2012

q: Who is the oldest person whose age has been verified, at what age did she die, and what 2018 claim disputed her record?
gold: Jeanne Calment, 122 years 164 days (died 1997); 2018 claim by Zak and Novoselov that her daughter Yvonne took her identity

q: Napoleon's height at his autopsy was recorded as 5 feet 2 inches. About how tall was he in metres, and why is the figure often misread?
gold: About 1.68 to 1.69 m (about 5 ft 6 to 5 ft 7 in imperial); the record used French pieds and pouces, which are longer than English feet and inches

q: The treaty that ended the War of 1812 was signed in a Belgian city. Was the Battle of New Orleans fought before or after the signing, and on what date was the battle?
gold: After: Treaty of Ghent signed 24 December 1814, battle on 8 January 1815

q: On what date in Coordinated Universal Time did Neil Armstrong first step onto the Moon, and at about what time UTC?
gold: 21 July 1969, about 02:56 UTC (20 July in US time zones)

q: Which Nobel laureate in Literature declined the prize of his own accord, and in what year? Another laureate is often named instead because he was forced to decline; who was that and when?
gold: Jean-Paul Sartre, 1964; Boris Pasternak was forced to decline in 1958

q: Which institution do Guinness World Records and UNESCO list as the oldest existing degree-granting university, in what year was it founded, and which European university is often named instead?
gold: University of al-Qarawiyyin, Fez, founded 859; Bologna (1088) is often named as the oldest

q: Python 1.0 came out in January 1994. In what year was Python first released to the public, and what was the version number?
The first iPhone was unveiled at Macworld in January 2007. On what date did it go on sale in the United States?
Who stole the Mona Lisa from the Louvre, in what year, and in what year was it recovered? Which famous painter was questioned as a suspect?
gold: Vincenzo Peruggia, 1911, recovered 1913 in Florence; Pablo Picasso was questioned

q: The kilogram was redefined in terms of the Planck constant. On what date was that vote held, and on what date did the new definition take effect?
gold: Voted 16 November 2018 at the 26th CGPM, in force 20 May 2019

q: Which country had a 30 February in its calendar, in what year, and why?
gold: Sweden, 1712, an extra day added to return to the Julian calendar after its gradual switch to the Gregorian went wrong

q: What is the lowest natural air temperature officially recorded at a weather station on Earth, where and when, and what lower figure from satellite data is sometimes cited?
gold: -89.2 C at Vostok Station, 21 July 1983; satellites measured about -93 to -98 C on the East Antarctic plateau

q: Counting overseas territories, which country spans the most time zones, and how many? Many sources name Russia; how many does Russia have?
gold: France, 12 (13 with its Antarctic claim); Russia has 11

q: In what year was the euro introduced as an accounting currency, and in what year did euro banknotes and coins enter circulation?
gold: 1999 as an accounting currency, 2002 notes and coins

q: The first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences won the second in which field and year? Her first was shared with whom?
gold: Chemistry, 1911 (Marie Curie); the 1903 Physics prize was shared with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel

q: The first nonstop transatlantic flight was made in 1919 by a crew of two. Who made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight, in what year, and what was the plane named?
gold: Charles Lindbergh, 1927, Spirit of St. Louis (Alcock and Brown flew the 1919 two-man flight)

q: The 1973 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to two negotiators of the Paris Peace Accords. Who declined it, and who accepted it?
gold: Le Duc Tho declined; Henry Kissinger accepted

q: Linus Torvalds announced his hobby operating system kernel on Usenet in August 1991. On what date was Linux version 0.01 released?
Which was the first self-governing country to grant all women the right to vote in national parliamentary elections, and in what year? Name one earlier territory sometimes cited instead.
gold: New Zealand, 1893; earlier cases include Wyoming Territory (1869), the Isle of Man (1881) and the Pitcairn Islands (1838)
